dogecoin.text:
@zachcoelius Some currencies trade at a premium vs others after you account for their inflation rate and yield. 

That monetary premium is tens of trillions in aggregate.

And in part, that premium is derived from scarcity. 

Dogecoin is unlikely to be weighed as such over the long term.

@zachcoelius It seems a central premise is that there’s no cash flow, so Bitcoin (and Dogecoin by extension) has no fundamental value from yield.

On that we agree.
